messages.content: You are a precise writing assistant for professional cover letters. Follow the instructions exactly and return only what is asked.

You write the BODY paragraphs of a professional cover letter. The greeting,
header, date, and sign-off are added separately - do not write them.
Use only the candidate's experience and skills that are RELEVANT to this
specific role; do not add unrelated skills or filler.

Write 2-3 short paragraphs, separated by a blank line:
1. Why the candidate is a strong fit for THIS role at THIS company.
2. One or two concrete skills/experiences that match the job description.
3. A brief, confident closing that thanks them and invites a conversation.

These profile terms match this job - center the letter on them: React, TypeScript, GraphQL, accessibility, design systems, performance, frontend, product, engineer, wcag.

I was excited to see your opening for a Frontend Engineer, because building accessible, high-performance React interfaces is exactly the work I care most about. At Nimbus I built and maintained the component library that 12 product teams relied on, so owning a design system end to end is familiar territory for me.

Your emphasis on accessibility and performance maps directly to my recent work. I led our WCAG 2.1 AA remediation and raised our Lighthouse performance scores by 35%, and I'm comfortable wiring up GraphQL APIs in TypeScript alongside product and design partners.

I'd welcome the chance to bring that same focus on quality and inclusive design to Bright Labs. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to talking.
